about: Registry of local SB 79 instruments (implementing / exemption / temporary-exclusion ordinances and TOD alternative plans) and HCD's review of each. Every entry rests on first-hand documents only: HCD's own letters, the jurisdiction's adopted ordinance or official web page, or the jurisdiction's own GIS layer. Each document listed was read for this registry. An entry marked `verification: "located"` cites a primary document that exists but could not be downloaded by script; confirm it by hand. Jurisdictions known from news or third-party trackers to have instruments, but without a primary document yet, are deliberately left out (see README).

rules.todap: A TOD alternative plan governs only if HCD has approved it (Gov. Code § 65912.161(d)).
rules.ordinance: An implementing, exemption, or temporary-exclusion ordinance governs unless HCD has found it out of compliance (HCD SB 79 page, 'TOD Project Compliance'). Statutory process: Gov. Code § 65912.160(d)(3)–(6).

instruments.title: Citywide TOD Alternative Plan (Ordinance 082-26, Planning Code § 207.11)

hcd.conditions: Compliance is contingent on the City not enforcing Planning Code § 207.11(b)(5), which barred State Density Bonus Law on alternative-plan sites.

coverage.note: Per HCD's letter, the plan redistributes SB 79 capacity across the City's TOD zones; § 65912.157 does not apply to sites covered by the plan until the next housing element.

instruments.title: Ordinance O-22099 — phasing the implementation of SB 79, including exemptions

local.reference: O-22099 (passed May 20, 2026; final passage May 21, 2026; effective 30 days after final passage)

hcd.note: No HCD findings letter on O-22099 has been located. Under § 65912.160(d)(3)(C), if HCD issues no written findings within its review period, the ordinance is deemed compliant for penalty purposes.

instruments.effectiveUntil: Fire, historic, and sea-level-rise sites: until a TOD alternative plan deemed compliant by HCD, or one year after the 7th-cycle housing element, whichever is first (§§ 4–6). Low-resource areas: no later than one year after the 7th-cycle housing element (§ 3).

coverage.note: § 4 phases in “all areas identified as being within a Very High Fire Severity Zone as determined by [CAL FIRE] pursuant to section 51178”, computed live from the State Fire Marshal's map. Not computed: § 2 (>1-mile walk; the City's map is not yet published), § 3 (low-resource areas), § 5 (historic resources), § 6 (one-foot sea-level rise).
